title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education
abstract: arXiv:2611.09177v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasing role in programming education, challenging traditional assessment methods as they can generate fully functional code instantly. This disrupts the reliability of student submissions as indicators of learning and effort. To address this issue, code provenance is essential for tracing the origins of code and distinguishing student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced components. We extend the Min-K% probability approach by incorporating synthetic non-member code generation and apply it to Python code for membership inference and provenance tracking. Evaluations cover free LLMs such as GPT-2, DistilGPT-2, and DialoGPT, as well as state-of-the-art commercial models including GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Mistral, DeepSeek, and LLaMA 3.3. tldr: 该论文提出了一种结合合成非成员代码生成的扩展Min-K%概率方法，用于追踪Python代码的来源并区分学生自创、AI生成和外部获取的代码，以维护编程教育中学生作业评估的可信度。
en_tdlr: This paper extends the Min-K% probability approach with synthetic non-member code generation to trace Python code provenance and distinguish student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced code, preserving the reliability of student assessment in programming education.
